title: Proposal: showEmojiPicker() on HTMLInputElement/HTMLTextareaElement

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
## Problem statement Most platforms today implement an emoji picker. For example:
OSX Windows Ubuntu iOS
However, there is no way to open it programmatically from a web page. Since many desktop users are not aware of the keyboard shortcut to open the emoji picker on their platform, it is common for websites to implement their own emoji picker, for example: Facebook | Twitter | Slack :-------------------------:|:-------------------------:|:------: ![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/175836/193887955-c39a85e6-5b81-4e12-92d1-b2c5d523df0c.png) | ![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/175836/193888074-04431938-35c0-41f2-9d9c-531b405f8fb4.png) | ![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/175836/193888239-82e2d945-a0db-486e-9861-6c5c19b7067a.png) The problem is that this is no trivial task: there are [over 3600 emojis](https://blog.emojipedia.org/whats-new-in-unicode-15-0/#:~:text=As%20of%20Emoji%2015.0%2C%20there,3%2C664%20emojis%20recommended%20by%20Unicode.), which become even more with variations etc. [Hundreds of packages](https://www.npmjs.com/search?q=emoji+picker) exist for this and [the extra page weight is measured in MB](https://nolanlawson.com/2020/06/28/introducing-emoji-picker-element-a-memory-efficient-emoji-picker-for-the-web/). Some websites simplify the task by ditching inclusivity and only including common emojis, without skin tone variations. As with most non-UA controls, accessibility often suffers. Others give up and just try to display the right shortcut to the user: The Web is [rife](https://splunktool.com/can-i-open-the-os-native-emoji-picker-in-a-web-page) [with](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55067185/can-i-open-the-os-native-emoji-picker-in-a-web-page) [authors](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71806158/how-to-open-emoji-keyboard-instead-of-alphabets-using-textinput-in-react-native) asking how to open the native emoji picker and being told this is not possible. ## Proposal [Past proposals](https://discourse.wicg.io/t/invoke-emoji-input/1030) centered around new input types or inputmodes. However, these are harder to reach consensus on, only cover a fraction of use cases, and involve more implementation effort. This proposal involves only a JS method analogous to [HTMLInputElement.showPicker()](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#dom-input-showpicker), which opens the underlying OS emoji picker if one is available. Sample IDL: ```webidl partial interface mixin ElementContentEditable { undefined showEmojiPicker(); }; ``` ### Alternatives considered Originally this proposed a more general `showCharacterPicker()` method with IDL like: ```webidl partial interface mixin ElementContentEditable { undefined showCharacterPicker(characterCategoryHint hint = "emoji"); }; enum characterCategoryHint { "emoji", "math", "letterlike", "bullets", "technical", "signs" }; ``` (The values in the enum above were inspired by the OSX character picker, but they're not essential for the proposal at all, I mainly included them as examples. This is framed as a hint because not every platform allows for this level of control when showing its picker. ) It was named `showCharacterPicker()` rather than `showEmojiPicker()` to be more future-proof and apply more generally. An optional argument can provide a hint about the type of character to be picked, and default to `"emoji"` but can also support other symbol categories. However, after some research into implementation, it appears emoji pickers are *far* more common than general character pickers in today's platforms. Regardless, it may still be a good idea to call it `showCharacterPicker()` or `showSymbolPicker()` to allow room for future expansion. ### Implementability Opening the OS emoji picker seems fairly straightforward in most platforms. Some examples: - On Windows, [there's `CoreInputViewKind.Emoji`](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51379524/open-emoji-panel-from-code-in-uwp-app). - On OSX, the way is to basically [programmatically fire the keyboard shortcut](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38611925/calling-the-emoji-symbols-picker-from-nsbutton-action) - In iOS, it may involve creating a hidden input field to catch the emoji, or changing the attributes of the textfield temporarily [like this](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/11382753/change-the-ios-keyboard-layout-to-emoji)

What if an OS picker is not available?

While rare, there are cases where the platform does not provide a character/emoji picker. For example, older platforms (Win < 10, Ubuntu < 18). I see several options here. In order of (my) preference: - Option 1: The UA polyfills it and provides an emoji picker (e.g. by bundling one of the existing emoji pickers). This would make the method more reliable and robust, and thus more likely to be used. To avoid increasing the footprint of the UA, perhaps it could be downloaded only when the browser is installed in platforms that require it? - Option 2 (thanks @pygy): The method is undefined on platforms that do not implement an emoji picker, which allows authors to handle lack of support for this API and lack of support for an emoji picker with the same code path. - Option 3: The method throws a `NotSupportedError` `DOMException`. Authors can feature detect this by using a `try ... catch` block. - Option 4: The function is a no-op, and we also provide a way to feature detect whether a picker is available so that any relevant UI can be hidden.
